page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. The configuration provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with two threads per core, 64 GB of total system memory, and a dedicated 402 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. It includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector instruction extensions, bfloat16, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. No dedicated graphics processing units are included in this machine profile.

Benchmark evaluation shows robust individual core capability, highlighted by strong top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core processing and Geekbench text processing workloads. Multithreaded execution across Geekbench, PassMark, and compilation tasks registers in the middle tier, aligning with standard hyperthreaded 8-core silicon footprints. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high throughput on cached 16 KB blocks at 1133.96 GB/sec, but uncached large-block transfers exhibit notable throughput constraints, dropping to 38.41 GB/sec for reads and 13.31 GB/sec for writes. Similarly, large-model language generation without discrete accelerators demonstrates lower throughput, recording 4.08 tokens per second on prompt processing for 70B parameter models.

The inclusion of a 402 GB local NVMe SSD provides low-latency ephemeral scratch space, making this instance economically efficient for I/O-intensive workloads that require standard compute-to-memory density without attaching external block volumes. Because memory bandwidth degrades on uncached operations, the instance exhibits a tradeoff where cache-friendly compute routines outperform raw memory-streaming operations. The platform is best matched for enterprise web serving, relational and key-value database operations such as Redis, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices requiring rapid local disk access.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, 64 GB of system memory, and 402 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage. Utilizing the x86_64 instruction set, the processor supports AVX-512, bfloat16, and accelerated cryptographic operations. Single-core integer and text-processing benchmarks demonstrate strong execution speed, while general multi-core compute tests deliver steady mid-range throughput. While small-block cached memory performance remains high, large-block uncached reads and writes face hardware-level bandwidth limits. Without discrete GPU accelerators, heavy matrix operations and large language model inference run slower than on specialized hardware. With a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio paired with fast local scratch storage, the instance delivers balanced cost efficiency for database engines, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD build environments, and containerized microservices.
